# Conditional Process Plan

Generates a clause installation plan combining configurable action connections with an optional conditional payment gate. It inherits `Connection Planning Functions`. Paths belong to the document where the clause executes; `{clauseKey}` denotes that clause's key.

`requestPolicy`, `policyAction`, `policyWatches` and `requestStep` have declarations but no implementations here. Their implementations determine the policy, payment action name, additional watched paths and generated request step. This shared definition therefore does not establish a particular payment request, actor or financial outcome.

## Conditional policy

`plan` first builds the inherited connection plan. The policy's `mode` defaults to `workflow`; only `mode: when` adds conditional gating. Any other returned mode leaves the connection plan unchanged.

For `when`, the action name returned by `policyAction` determines an `Allowed` field under `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}` and a corresponding `Gate` field in `/paymentTerms`. The planned initial `Allowed` value is `false`; the `Gate` field stores its path. A different existing gate path rejects planning with `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`. An absent runtime flag remains unknown; the planned initialization is not evidence that it has run.

Generated handlers reevaluate the gate on paths returned by `policyWatches` and on document paths found in the policy's `when` expression. The gate becomes true only when all three checks pass:

- `/activation/active` equals `true`.
- `/clauses/documentSources` is absent, or `/sourceLinks/ready` equals `true`.
- The `when` expression evaluates to exactly `true`.

The flag is updated only when its value changes. Each handler then executes the step produced by `requestStep(gate, policy)`, including when the gate did not change. Whether that step emits or suppresses a request is not defined here. An allowed flag is neither payment completion nor a grant of personal authority.

`parameters.sources` defaults to an empty object and declares aliases used by predicate paths beginning `/sources/`. A nonempty map also adds an Embedded Node Channel handler using the same gate and request steps; no `sourcePath` filter is assigned to that channel here.

Predicate dependencies must be statically inspectable. `$document` operands must be literal, non-root paths beginning `/`; `/sources/` aliases must be declared. `$nodeBlueId` must directly wrap an object containing only `$document`. Supported expression keys are `$document`, `$nodeBlueId`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract`, `$literal`, `list` and `val`. Contents of `$literal` are not scanned. Unsupported keys, dynamic paths, undeclared aliases and nesting remaining after 33 scan passes reject planning.

`validateConfiguration` invokes inherited connection validation and `requestPolicy`. `validateTransition` always rejects with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

## Inherited action connections

`defaultBindings` are overlaid by explicit clause `bindings`. Property bindings must be declared in `bindingTypes`, match their declared kind, and be present unless listed in `optionalBindings`. A `pointer` binding must be a non-root path. Action and `childActions` bindings are distinguished from property bindings. `embeds` and `embedsCollections` require declared pointer bindings. `initialState` supplies object initial values at named pointer bindings. `snapshotBindings` capture existing bound values during planning; a supplied snapshot path with no value is rejected.

Actions come from `type/actions`, or `parameters/actions` when `configurableActions` is true. Without actions, an object `initialState` is required. Unless `readParametersFromDocument` is true, generated actions receive captured `parameters` with `actions` and `conditions` removed. When it is true, the generated parameters constant is empty; this planner does not itself perform a replacement runtime read. Executable configuration remains unevaluated during planning.

Each action binding is a dictionary of named connections. `on` supports `workflow`, `event`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `channel`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer`. Sources select calls, events, embedded-document events or document changes. `initialized` selects `Clauses Initialized`; `activated` selects `Document Activated`. `path` selects document or embedded locations, and collection handlers additionally restrict events to descendants of their configured path. Embedded sources request processing of their target or collection unless `embed` is false. A workflow selects its channel using `party` when supplied, otherwise `channel`, and can declare `request` and `event`. Declaring a workflow does not establish a particular caller's permission.

Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no dot, slash or tilde. An action's `automatic` connection occupies reserved name `_automatic`; `pathBinding`, when present there, resolves through property bindings. Unsupported connection fields, unknown condition action names and duplicate workflow names are rejected.

Connection `params` override action `defaults`; both default to empty objects. `when` defaults to true and `once` to false. A consumed `once` connection, an out-of-scope collection event or a false connection `when` stops that invocation. Argument validation, action `require/when` and `parameters.conditions` can reject it. A configured preflight must return `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` continues through `before` and the action's `do`. With `resultContract: outcome-v1`, the action must also return one of those outcomes, and only `acceptedNew` proceeds through `after` and consumes `once`. The default `legacy` result contract adds no such outcome requirement. `before` and `after` default to empty lists.

Each connection has `armed` and `fired` fields under `/connectionState_{clauseKey}`, keyed by its action name joined to its connection name with a dot. Both have planned initial value false. `fired` is set true only when a `once` connection reaches its final step; it records connection consumption, not confirmation of an external result.

## Timer connections

A timer requires exactly one of `timestamp` and `afterEvent`. An absolute `timestamp` is an integer Unix instant in microseconds, from 0 through 9007199254740991, and arms on clause initialization. It cannot specify `delayMs` or `policy`. A relative timer uses a timestamped `afterEvent` source and a positive integer `delayMs`, at most 9007199254740 milliseconds; initialization cannot supply that source. The generated deadline uses the source's logical timestamp and the delay converted to microseconds, and must remain within the timestamp range.

Relative `policy` defaults to `first`; `latest` is the other supported value. `first` suppresses further arming once `armed` is true. `latest` emits a replacement request using the same timer key. Arming sets `armed` true and emits a Timer Request carrying the captured trigger. Neither firing nor cancellation clears `armed` in this implementation, so it is an arming latch, not proof that a timer remains pending. `once` also prevents rearming after `fired` becomes true. Optional `cancelOn` must name a nonempty supported source and emits a keyed Cancel Timer Request.

Timer effects require the selected Time runtime and become effective only after commit. A request is not a firing. New deadlines must follow the invocation's logical timestamp; a new standalone document without a prior external position can initialize with an elapsed absolute deadline. Processing may occur late while retaining the requested deadline's logical timestamp. Cancellation affects a still-pending registration in logical input order and cannot undo an earlier firing.
